samples.marker: ScreenConnect File Manager: stock helper; revoked signer retained
evidence: Byte-for-byte SHA-256 match to filC1D18007D3175279B0EDD654D18B0CA5 in independently downloaded ScreenConnect_25.2.4.9229_Release.msi (MSI SHA-256 0dabef8ee019bc34bf315794df0f5321ee8122e18d87411ab5f79f6ef73f46a0).
Parsed all managed methods with dnfile/dncil and decompiled with ILSpy. CLR entry point is Program.Main, token 0x06000006. No manifest resources, embedded relay parameters or payload archive.

Main sets up exception logging, visual styles, thread-local WH_GETMESSAGE and WH_CALLWNDPROCRET hooks, and SetWinEventHook scoped to the current thread. Callbacks forward mouse-wheel events, customize shell menus, draw menu items and resize/hide file-dialog controls. These are GUI operations, not a keystroke recorder.

Reads ProfilesDirectory from the local-machine ProfileList registry key and uses ILCreateFromPath/SHCreateItemFromIDList to select the file-browser root. Creates IFileOpenDialog, labels it ScreenConnect File Manager and shows it.

OnFileOk obtains the selected shell item's display path and passes it to Process.Start(new ProcessStartInfo(path) { UseShellExecute = true }). The launched item is selected through the browser; no fixed command, downloader, persistence installation or outbound channel appears in this helper.

Fetched same-version ScreenConnect.Core and ScreenConnect.Windows dependencies from the MSI. Traced startup helpers: FixupAppDomain is empty; FixupProcess restricts DLL search to System32 and sets image-load mitigation. Logging helpers register ordinary application/AppDomain exception handlers.

Authenticode content digest and signer cryptography verify. Independently downloaded DigiCert CRL verifies against the embedded issuer certificate (openssl crl -verify: verify OK); serial 0B9360051BCCF66642998998D5BA97CE is revoked, with Key Compromise reason and effective date 2022-08-17. Retain the accurate suspicious certificate trait; cryptographic integrity does not establish current trust.

Fetched Triage overview, static1 and behavioral1 reports. Overall/static score 8 comes from revoked/untrusted certificate signatures. Behavioral score is 3. The process tree contains the helper and .NET dw20.exe crash reporter; listed API/registry heuristics are not proof of an implant. Reported request/TCP/UDP counts for the helper are zero. No local sample execution was performed.
samples.why_collected: External detections primarily identify RemoteAdmin, ConnectWise riskware or hacktool functionality, and the sandbox explicitly scores the revoked signer. These are concrete reasons for collection, but do not show abuse of this stock helper. The exact vendor comparison and GUI execution trace tip the file-level verdict toward BENIGN; queue guidance still routes it to sighted quarantine.
missing_context: Operator authorization and endpoint execution history

samples.marker: LuaJIT 2.1 beta3: standard interpreter; no embedded payload
evidence: Rizin execution tracing starts at 0x4014e0 through MinGW CRT initialization to main at 0x461b50. Main creates a Lua state, supplies argc/argv to the protected pmain callback at 0x4021a0, reports errors, closes the state and returns status.

pmain parses normal -e/-l/-b/-j/-O/-i/-v/-E options, constructs the Lua arg table, opens standard libraries, processes LUA_INIT and runs the supplied script or REPL/stdin. At 0x402794 it calls getenv(LUA_INIT); @-prefixed values select a file and other values select source text. -E sets LUA_NOENV and skips environment initialization. There is no hard-coded bootstrap script or operator endpoint in this path.

Fetched the referenced luajit.org homepage and upstream LuaJIT frontend source. Its command-line, initialization and error-handling model agrees with the disassembly; this is a behavioral comparison, not a claim of an exact reproducible build.

Traced system at 0x44e398: its argument comes from the Lua stack string helper, implementing os.execute rather than running a built-in command. Dynamic native-module loading and FFI implement the interpreter's advertised capabilities.

VirtualProtect at 0x429f5e changes the JIT machine-code area; nearby paths switch write/execute protection. The CreateThread call at 0x40cc04 starts the profiler worker after resolving winmm timeBeginPeriod/timeEndPeriod. TLS callbacks and constructor pointers implement MinGW runtime initialization and cleanup.
TerminateProcess at 0x45ede9 receives GetCurrentProcess() and status 0xc0000409 in the CRT failure path, followed by abort. This is self-termination, not defender-process targeting.

The 4693-byte trailing region begins at the COFF symbol-table offset 506368 and contains symbol/string records. No appended executable archive or embedded Lua/LuaJIT bytecode chunk was found. Sections, constant tables and runtime library registration account for the image; no payload decoder or unrelated tasking routine was identified.
Unsigned binary, future header timestamp and executable-memory APIs are retained as factual observations. They do not independently prove a maliciously modified interpreter.
samples.why_collected: The single named detection explicitly says RiskWare.MisusedLegit.LuaJIT. The external malware provenance and negative votes may reflect an interpreter shipped with a malicious script or wrapper, but those artifacts are absent. The standard startup/execution paths and absence of an embedded malicious program tip this standalone file toward BENIGN, without establishing that its original deployment was authorized.
missing_context: Original command line and LUA_INIT environment
Adjacent native modules, launch wrapper and deployment telemetry

samples.marker: Node.js ts5.7 types: exact npm declarations; no runtime code
evidence: Read the complete 5437-byte file and inspected extracted/decoded facts. It contains license/comments and TypeScript triple-slash lib/path references only: no executable statement, import-time action, decoder or network call.
Fetched @types/node 25.9.1 from npm. node/ts5.7/index.d.ts has the exact submitted SHA-256. Its relative references resolve into the expected Node/TypeScript declaration set in that package.

Inspected the fetched package's declaration dependencies and manifest: main is empty, scripts is empty, and the package dependency is undici-types >=7.24.0 <7.24.7. Fetched and inspected satisfying undici-types 7.24.6: declaration/documentation files, no JavaScript/native/shell payload, no scripts and no further package dependencies.
The Node.js GitHub documentation URL is a license attribution in a comment. Names such as child_process, crypto and net refer to type declarations, and do not invoke those facilities.
samples.why_collected: No hostile behavior is present in these exact upstream declarations. Collection as a member/dependency of a hostile package or inheritance of a containing bundle's label is plausible; the original container was not supplied, so that explanation remains an inference.
missing_context: Original containing package and collection context

trait_changes: Add notable SetWinEventHook API-name observation under ui/window/hook, without asserting keylogging or global hooks.
Add notable bytecode-output CLI help observation under ui/help and require it with existing LuaJIT banner/runtime evidence for a distinct CLI interpreter identity.
Correct RMM ProductName description to say remote-administration software: a vendor helper is not necessarily an unattended agent.
Retain all accurate capability and provenance findings, including the one suspicious revoked-certificate observation. No hostile detections are justified.

verification.analysis: atomscan and cleave facts run for each original full path; ILSpy/dncil and Rizin supplied independent execution-path inspection.
verification.focused_controls: Original samples match the new rules. Equal-length scratch PE mutations removing the LuaJIT banner or bytecode-help wording break the CLI identity; removing SetWinEventHook breaks only the new API-name observation.
verification.rescans: All three original samples rescanned with atomscan after new trait additions: File Manager retains one suspicious trait and zero hostile; LuaJIT and declarations have zero suspicious or hostile. File Manager rescanned again after the RMM description correction.
verification.final_gate: make validate is run as the final action after verdict markers; its exit result is reported separately.
